scope: Synthetic in-process data-structure comparison; not a full solver RSS qualification
baseline_definition: One node owns lower and upper Bound vectors, an optional copied BasisState vector, and a copied local-cut vector. This reproduces the former queued-node payload shape; it is not a comparison to another solver.
current_definition: Each node owns BranchNode plus a one-delta NodeBounds, and shares one immutable BasisState and one copy-on-write NodeCuts payload. Root model and per-worker bound buffers are held in both modes.
measure: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss, Linux KiB, one process per run; runs executed sequentially
safety_budget: The benchmark rejects estimated baseline payloads above 1 GiB and dimensions above per-argument caps; an oversized-input rejection was exercised.
limitations: The benchmark constructs data structures, not actual branch-and-bound solves.
Every current node has a single delta; deep-path materialization and shared-chain retention are not measured.
The root matrix is a fixed 1024-nonzero diagonal matrix and the four worker buffers are bound vectors only.
Allocator metadata, full solver workspaces, cut generation, concurrent workers, and OS/device memory pressure are not isolated.
RSS depends on this Linux allocator/runtime and Debug binary; repeat on release builds and supported deployment hosts.
conclusion: In this controlled structure-only case, baseline peak RSS grows with queued copied payloads while current RSS remains near the fixed process/root/worker footprint through 4000 nodes. This supports the direction of the W01 representation but does not close IR-19; full-solver allocation and frontier/RSS scaling remain required.
